brief: Nvidia reports fiscal Q3 results tonight with interim CEO Colette Kress after Jensen Huang's resignation, a stock down roughly 35% from its October high having shed about $2 trillion in market cap, new export curbs covering Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia, and a newly closed China cloud-rental loophole. Street consensus sees revenue of $109.3 billion against the company's own $108 billion guide, but the buyside bar sits higher: JPMorgan's survey puts revenue at $112.6 billion and UBS's Arcuri expects a $3-4 billion beat plus a roughly $130 billion Q4 guide, so a merely in-line Street number would read as a disappointment. The real debate is not the quarter but whether Kress reaffirms last quarter's 70% revenue-growth guide for next fiscal year under new export rules and leadership uncertainty; BofA puts 10-15% odds that guidance gets pulled entirely until a permanent CEO is named. Options price an 8% move, the richest in two years, though realized moves have usually undershot implied ones historically. Beyond tonight, Goldman and Deutsche Bank frame the bigger question as what multiple the market should put on Nvidia's 2028-2031 earnings, while UBS and SemiAnalysis have each cut their 2028 estimates.
